ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.** A level-1 Shugyosha does Light ×0.5 / Balanced ×1.0 / Heavy ×1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's *reach* also scales ×0.5→×0.9.
text: RR:155 packs two different formulas into one sentence and gets the pairing backwards. In web v0.717 DAMAGE (§1t99s0§.as:3255-3271) light scales with light mastery (0.5 -> 0.9), balanced with balanced mastery (1.0 -> 1.2), and heavy is FLAT x1.4 with no mastery term at all - :3267-3270 fall through three cases to '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;'. REACH (§1t99s0§.as:3091-3121) is the mirror image: light is FLAT x1.4 of base (:3094), balanced scales with balanced mastery (:3105), and heavy scales with heavy mastery (:3116) AND is clamped to a floor of 100 at :3117-3119. So exactly one of the three stances is mastery-flat in each table, and it is a different stance in each. The ledger's '(Heavy is fixed)' is true for damage only, and its 'Heavy's reach also scales x0.5 -> x0.9' is right but is the ONLY reach term it names.

The frame shows otherwise: in t1003.000.png the CANNOT CHANGE STANCE label is PALE GREY, distinctly not the saturated yellow of the '150% DAMAGE' line directly beneath it, and its bar carries NO numerals at all - the numeric bars are the green HP (14/20) and blue Chi (31/31) ABOVE it. The notes conflated the third bar with the HP bar and the label colour with the buff banner's. The code agrees with the frame: §1t113s0§.as:111 builds the label at '#BBBBBB', and §1t5205s0§ sets only bar.scaleX with no text, while the numeric bars are set by §1t5202s0§ at :319-324.

text: The war-map board specification is NOT android-only, which was the one real hole in the packet's world finding. Web v0.717 §1t7934s0§.as:15/:17/:19 declare 8 / 21 / 51 — byte-identical to WarSelectUI.as — :232 is the land test `getPixel(param1 + §1t12536s0§ - §1t12535s0§, param2 + §1t12537s0§) != 0`, and :299-300 place the war flag at `(x + 21) * 10 + 4.5` / `(y + 51) * 10 + 8.8`. §1t6481s0§.as:17/:19/:21 repeats the same three constants for the world map. The 63x72 mask itself is web bindata 92 (reference/extracted/bindata/92_1t4648s0.bin), not an android blob. So the C2 build-parity caveat does not apply to the war map: geography, bounds, offsets and pitch are all attested on the WEB side.

text: A genuine, non-circular web/android parity datum - rare in this corpus, and it survives correction C2. reference/extracted/bindata/92_1t4648s0.bin (a WEB payload bindata file) and reference/extracted/android/110_Mobile_MapBitmapData.bin (the ANDROID blob) have the identical md5 13068dfa1a5cc5628720a25782f93fed. Both are a GIF89a 63x72 with exactly 735 white and 3801 black pixels. C2's circularity warning does not apply here, because 92 is a web-side artifact and 110 is android-side - this is not a file diffed against itself. Android WarSelectUI.as:153 wires it to the war board via QuestEngine.getMapBitmapData(), and Mobile_MapBitmapData.as:5 embeds 110 by name, so the file's role is named by the game, not inferred.
